 A natural analogy for these intertwined crises was furnished by the dramatic rising in
the second half of October of a powerful west wind, signal that autumn was passing into
winter. The meteorologist F. H. Ludlam’s close examination of the Ode (in Weather xxvii
(1972) 503–14) concludes that its images derive from a singularly accurate observation of
the travelling cyclonic thunderstorm that typically accompanies the abrupt onset of the
Mediterranean winter. This is not to say that S. observed all the atmospheric details in the
